newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares in highest rise in two weeks.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares in highest rise in two weeks.

text.p: Egyptian share prices on Tuesday scored their highest rise in two weeks.
The Capital Market Authority overall index closed 1.93 points higher at 339.43, the highest level since August 5, in below-average trade of 39.96 million pounds ($11.8 million).
"The number of shares which went up were almost double the number of shares that went down. This is a good indicator," Shawkat Raslan of Prime Investments told Reuters.
"The whole market is going up, but slowly. Most people in the market now are long-term (investors)," he added.
The blue-chip Abu Qir Fertilisers and Chemical Industries performed well, ending 2.95 pounds up at 77.61 but volume was a relatively low 783,000 pounds.

"The volume was low because shareholders do not want to sell, particularly after the firm announced it was allowed to export fertilizers after a two-year ban, increasing profits by 15 percent," Raslan said.
Suez Cement, a favourite in the cement sector, was among the busiest stocks of the day, with 3.4 million pounds of trade. The equity rose 0.38 pounds to 64.82.
The company's GDRs which trade on the London stock exchange are priced at a higher level and this makes the local share attractive, Raslan said.
"The problem with this firm is that there is a large number of shares in the market and that's why it moves very slowly," he added.
A strong performance by Housing and Development Bank pushed its share up 1.89 pounds to clost at 87.89.
"It was reported that the bank made 31.9 million pounds of profits in the first six months of this year against about 42 million in the whole of 1996," Raslan said.
Egyptian Electro Cables was a victim of a government announcement that an anchor investor was sought to buy the firm's shares, still held by the state, at 110 pounds a share, Raslan said.
The equity shed 1.33 pounds to end at 99.14. "I expect it to continue falling," he added.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 470.08 points from 462.71 points on Monday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 249.62 from 249.47.
Of the 83 shares traded, 49 rose, 22 ended lower and 12 remained unchanged.
